newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European bourses break records, boosted by US.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European bourses break records, boosted by US.

text.p: London, Frankfurt, Paris and several other European bourses surged to record highs in early trade on Thursday, boosted by a 93-point advance on Wall Street overnight which more than erased its losses of the previous day.

By 0930 GMT London was up more than half a percent, Frankfurt was up 1.7 percent in electronic trading and the Paris bourse was up 1.3 percent. All were at new record index highs and other European stock markets chalked up similar gains.

"We've really gone roaring up," one London dealer said. "Wall Street was good, the results have been good, it's shaping up to be a cracking day. The only problem would be if the early mark-up keeps buyers away."

Wall Street's recovery came after the second half of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony on the U.S. economy reversed some of the damage wreaked on Wall Street last week by his warnings on equity prices.

Instead of repeating last week's comment that Wall Street's ascent "raised questions of sustainability", Greenspan on Wednesday appeared to soften his tone, saying the stock market was "properly priced" if Wall Street's assumptions about corporate profit growth proved correct.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average powered ahead on his comments, ending 93 points higher at 6,946.
On currency markets the dollar continued to set 34-month highs against the German mark in early trading, reaching a peak of 1.7193 marks after the release of February German unemployment data.
Unemployment rose to a seasonally-adjusted 4.316 million in February, an increase of 5,000 from January. The unemployment rate, based on unadjusted data, was unchanged at 12.2 percent.
